sentences.text: The extinct genus Tsoabichi translates to "monster" in the Shoshone language and is a member of the caimanine crocodylians.
Unlike modern relatives, this animal lacked a bony ridge between the eyes but had three smaller ridges separating the eye sockets.
The skull table featured a supraoccipital bone that formed a distinct V-shape.
Its back armor consisted of wider dorsal osteoderms, some of which bore two keels on the outer surface.
The underside of the body possessed ventral osteoderms that were split into two parts.
Paleontologist Christopher A. Brochu named and described the genus Tsoabichi in 2010, designating Tsoabichi greenriverensis as the type species.
Fossils of Tsoabichi come from the Green River Formation in Wyoming and date to the Ypresian stage of the Eocene.
Tsoabichi lived during the Ypresian stage, approximately 56 to 48.07 million years ago.

It is debated whether Tsoabichi originated in North America or South America, though researchers suggest it likely came from a South American population that reentered North America in the Early Eocene.
